_readme: SINGLE SOURCE for every FAQ on the site. _build/regen.mjs emits BOTH the
visible <details> accordion and the FAQPage JSON-LD from these strings, so
the visible answer and acceptedAnswer.text are byte-identical by
KEY = the route the FAQ belongs to ('' = home, 'pricing/' = /pricing).
HARD RULE: answers are PLAIN TEXT. No HTML, and none of the characters
& < > " — they would break the byte-identity between the HTML and the JSON.
regen.mjs fails loudly if one appears.

items.q: Will paint protection film turn yellow?
items.a: No. Both films we install are TPU, not the old PVC film that yellowed in the sun. Essential is {{film:essential.film}} and Signature is {{film:signature.film}}, and each carries its manufacturer's own warranty against yellowing, cracking and staining. {{terms:warranty}}

items.q: Does the film really heal its own scratches?
items.a: Yes, within limits. The top coat is self-healing: swirl marks and light wash scuffs close up with heat from the sun or warm water. A deep gouge that cuts right through the film does not heal - but it stopped at the film instead of at your paint, which is the point.

items.q: What exactly does the warranty cover?
items.a: {{terms:warranty}} The film manufacturer covers the film itself against defects such as yellowing, cracking, bubbling and delamination. Our year covers the installation: lifting edges, trapped dirt, anything that is our work rather than the film.

items.q: How long does the car stay with you?
items.a: One to three days for most cars, depending on coverage. A partial front or full front is usually a single day. Track Pack and full body need two to three, because every panel is decontaminated and inspected before any film is laid. The exact number of days for your car comes with the quote.

items.q: How do I look after a filmed car?
items.a: Wash it like paint, just more gently. Hand wash with a pH-neutral shampoo, keep a pressure washer off the film edges, and leave polishes, waxes and anything abrasive out of it. A ceramic top-up over fresh film makes washing easier again: {{from:ceramic-topup}}.

items.q: Can the film be removed later?
items.a: Yes - film is designed to come off. With heat and slow, controlled pulling it lifts away without taking the clear coat with it, which is exactly why owners film a car before they sell it. Film left on long past its warranty life gets harder to remove, so do not leave a failing panel on the car.

items.q: How much does a car wrap cost in Boca Raton?
items.a: Chrome delete starts at {{price:chrome-delete}}, a full color change at {{price:color-change}}, and a Signature wrap in a premium or color-shift film at {{price:signature-wrap}}. {{terms:fromMeaning}} {{terms:tax}}

items.q: Which wrap films do you use?
items.a: For a full color change we install 3M 2080 and Avery Dennison SW900 in gloss, satin or matte. Signature wraps use premium film: Inozetek Super Gloss, KPMF and color-shift finishes. Over 150 colors across those brands. {{terms:warranty}}

items.q: Does a wrap damage the paint underneath?
items.a: No. Vinyl is removed with controlled heat, and on factory paint in good condition the surface underneath is left as it was on the day of installation. Repainted or already damaged panels are assessed one by one before we start, and we say so before you book if a panel is not a candidate.

items.q: Can you wrap only part of the car?
items.a: Yes. Roof, mirrors, spoiler, stripes and one-off requests are quoted individually: {{price:accents}}. A chrome delete covers window trim, grille surround and badges {{from:chrome-delete}}, and it is the cheapest way to change how the car reads from the front.

items.q: Should I wrap the car or protect it with PPF?
items.a: A wrap changes how the car looks. Paint protection film is optically clear and protects the paint underneath, with full front from {{price:full-front.essential}} in NAR Essential film. The two combine on the same car, and we quote them together so you can see both numbers before deciding.

items.q: How much does a ceramic coating cost in Boca Raton?
items.a: Two prices, both published. The 3-Year Ceramic Package on bare paint starts at {{price:ceramic-3yr}}. Over fresh paint protection film or a wrap, the top-up starts at {{price:ceramic-topup}}. {{terms:fromMeaning}} {{terms:tax}}

items.q: What does the 3-Year Ceramic Package include?
items.a: Decon, single-stage gloss prep, coating, cure. The prep is the part that decides the result: a coating locks in whatever is under it, so the paint is cleaned and corrected before anything is sealed onto it. The car goes back to you once the coating has cured, not straight off the bench.

items.q: Can a ceramic coating go over PPF or a wrap?
items.a: Yes, and it is the usual pairing. Ceramic over fresh film gives you the beading and the easier washing without touching the paint underneath, and it makes the whole car behave the same way instead of half film and half bare panel. That is the top-up, from {{price:ceramic-topup}}.

items.q: Does a ceramic coating replace paint protection film?
items.a: No. A coating adds gloss, water beading and easier washing, but it is microns thick and it will not stop a stone chip. For impact protection you need film: {{startingAt:ppf}}. Film on the front end and ceramic over the rest is how most cars leave the studio.

items.q: Do I need paint correction before the coating?
items.a: Some, always. The 3-Year Ceramic Package includes a single-stage gloss prep for exactly that reason. Heavier swirls, holograms or etching are a separate paint correction job, from {{price:paint-correction}}, and it is worth doing first because a coating seals in every defect it goes over.

items.q: How much does detailing cost in Boca Raton?
items.a: There are two services and two numbers. An Interior Detail starts at {{price:interior}} and a Paint Correction, one to two stage, starts at {{price:paint-correction}}. {{terms:fromMeaning}} {{terms:tax}}

items.q: What is included in the interior detail?
items.a: A full interior strip-down, hot extraction of carpets and upholstery, and leather cleaned and fed. Every panel, vent and seam is steamed and agitated, trim and glass are finished by hand, and the car goes back with nothing left to wipe. Vehicle size and how much has built up are what move the final number, and we confirm it at intake before any work starts.

items.q: What does paint correction do, and how many stages do I need?
items.a: Correction is machine polishing that removes defects rather than hiding them. Stage 1 cuts, levelling swirls, scratches and oxidation. Stage 2 refines away the haze that cutting leaves. Stage 3 is a final jewelling pass for a show finish. The listed price covers one to two stages, which is what most daily-driven cars need, and a third stage is quoted separately when the clear coat asks for it. Gloss is read with a meter before and after, so the result is a number: a typical neglected panel goes from about 42 GU on arrival to about 94 GU after correction. It is also the right prep step before a ceramic coating, so the finish is sealed at its best rather than as found.

items.q: Are these the real prices, or a starting point to get me on the phone?
items.a: Real prices. {{terms:fromMeaning}} {{terms:tax}}

items.q: Why does PPF have two prices on every line?
items.a: Because you choose the film. Essential is NAR H190 PPF: self-healing 7.5-mil TPU with a 10-year film warranty. Signature is 3M Scotchgard Pro Series 200, the 3M flagship. Partial Front is {{price:partial-front.essential}} in Essential and {{price:partial-front.signature}} in Signature; Full Front is {{price:full-front.essential}} and {{price:full-front.signature}}. Same prep, same installers, same installation warranty — the film is the only difference.

items.q: What would move my quote away from the number on this page?
items.a: Vehicle size, panel shape and paint condition. A large SUV takes more film than a sedan, deep contours take longer to lay, and paint that needs correction before a coating adds work. Send the make, model and year and you get the exact figure for that car.

items.q: What is not priced on this page?
items.a: Roof, mirrors, spoilers, stripes and one-off requests are quoted per car, because the panel count and the shapes decide the price. Everything else we sell today is listed above, grouped by service: paint protection film {{startingAt:ppf}}, wraps {{startingAt:wraps}}, ceramic coating {{startingAt:ceramic}}, window tint {{startingAt:tint}}, detailing {{startingAt:detailing}}.

items.q: Which paint protection films do you actually install?
items.a: Two, and both are named on every quote. Signature is {{film:signature.film}} - {{film:signature.note}}. Essential is {{film:essential.film}} - {{film:essential.note}}. Both are self-healing TPU and both go on to the same protocol, in the same bay, by the same installer.

items.q: Is NAR a worse film than 3M?
items.a: It is a different price, not a different class of film. Both are self-healing TPU with a manufacturer warranty behind them. Full Front is {{price:full-front.essential}} in NAR against {{price:full-front.signature}} in 3M, and that difference comes off your invoice rather than into our margin. {{terms:fromMeaning}}

items.q: Why will you not fit a cheaper film?
items.a: Because we would be the ones refitting it. Budget paint protection film is usually TPH, a hybrid material engineered down to a price rather than the TPU both of our films are made from. Under sustained Florida sun and heat that category is reported to haze, lift at the edges and turn amber within roughly 6 to 18 months, and there is rarely a manufacturer left standing behind the warranty.

items.q: What does the warranty actually cover?
items.a: {{terms:warranty}} The manufacturer warranty covers the film itself against defects such as yellowing, cracking and delamination, under that manufacturer's own published terms. The SERRES installation warranty covers our work for a year: lifting edges, trapped debris, alignment. Bring the car back and we refit the affected panel.

items.q: Why is a Barcelona studio opening in Boca Raton?
items.a: Because South Florida is harder on paint than Barcelona is: year-round UV, salt air, love bugs and rock chips off I-95. The protocol we built in Barcelona was designed for exactly that kind of punishment, so we are bringing it over intact instead of starting again. Same two films, same warranty terms: {{terms:warranty}}

items.q: When does the Boca Raton studio open?
items.a: In two stages. Detailing services open on {{business:openingSoftLabel}}, and the full paint protection film launch follows on {{business:openingFullLabel}}. The exact street address is announced in October 2026.

items.q: What does the SERRES protocol actually change?
items.a: Six fixed steps on every car, whatever it costs: paint thickness gauged at intake, a HEPA-filtered bay, anti-static prep, a filtered-air dry, gloss measured before and after correction, and a photo record of every stage. None of it is an optional extra and none of it is reserved for expensive cars.

We price it against the published list and answer with one exact figure, not a range. {{terms:fromMeaning}}

A full front is {{price:full-front.essential}} or {{price:full-front.signature}}, and full body is {{price:full-body.essential}} or {{price:full-body.signature}}. A partial front is {{price:partial-front.essential}} in NAR H190 or {{price:partial-front.signature}} in 3M Scotchgard Pro Series 200, and a full front is {{price:full-front.essential}} and {{price:full-front.signature}}. {{terms:fromMeaning}} {{terms:tax}} {{terms:warranty}}

items.q: What does PPF cost for a Fort Lauderdale car?
items.a: The same published list as everyone else: {{startingAt:ppf}} for a partial front in NAR H190, and {{price:full-front.essential}} for a full front in Essential. Nothing is added for the drive up. {{terms:tax}}

items.q: Does the salt air off the water reach the paint?
items.a: Yes, and it does not need spray to do it. A car kept near the Intracoastal picks up a salt film that pulls moisture out of the night air, holds it against the clear coat and works into every stone chip. Rinsing salt off film is easier than polishing etching out of paint. {{terms:warranty}}

items.q: How far is the studio from Pompano Beach?
items.a: Closer than anywhere else we cover. The studio is in the Boca Raton and Pompano Beach area, so the run in is I-95 north from the Atlantic Boulevard or Copans Road ramp, or Federal Highway the whole way. The exact address and a measured drive time are published in October 2026.

items.q: Which PPF coverage suits a Pompano Beach car?
items.a: It depends which road the car lives on. An I-95 commuter past Copans Road collects chips on the hood and fender tops, so Full Front at {{price:full-front.essential}} is the honest answer. A car that mostly does Federal Highway plazas and the Citi Centre lot picks up bumper corners and mirror caps, and Partial Front at {{price:partial-front.essential}} covers that.

items.q: What exactly do the first thirty cars get?
items.a: Three things: 15% off any paint protection film or wrap, a free ceramic top-up over the fresh film, normally {{price:ceramic-topup}}, and Founding Member status, which is 10% off detailing for life. The discount is locked to the price list in force on the day you book. {{terms:fromMeaning}}

items.q: Is the deposit refundable, and what happens to it?
items.a: It is refundable in full until work begins on your car, and it is applied to your final invoice rather than charged on top. The amount is {{business:depositUsd}} US dollars. No card details are taken on this site: we send a secure deposit link by text or email once your slot is confirmed. {{terms:tax}}

items.q: Can I reserve more than one car?
items.a: One car per reservation, so thirty slots stay thirty cars. If you want a second car in the Founders Club, send a second reservation and we will confirm whether a slot is still open for it. Every car booked this way carries the same cover as any other job here: {{terms:warranty}}

items.q: How much is window tint in Boca Raton?
items.a: A full car in ceramic film is {{startingAt:tint}} — every side window plus the rear glass. {{terms:fromMeaning}} {{terms:tax}}

items.q: What tint is legal in Florida?
items.a: On a sedan the front side windows have to let at least 28% of light through, and the back sides and rear window at least 15%. On an SUV or van the front sides are the same 28%, while the back sides and rear window can go down to 6%. The windshield takes a transparent strip above the AS-1 line only, and a state medical exemption exists for drivers who need darker. Those figures are Florida Statutes 316.2953 and 316.2954; bring us the vehicle and we measure the glass before anything is cut.

items.q: Is ceramic film worth it over a cheap dyed tint?
items.a: Ceramic film rejects infrared — the part of sunlight you feel as heat — without having to be darker, and it carries no metal, so GPS, cell signal and a toll transponder are unaffected. A dyed film only darkens the glass, and it fades. That is why the one tint we fit is ceramic.

items.q: When can I roll the windows down after a tint?
items.a: Not straight away. The film has to bond to the glass first, and moving a window before it has set can lift an edge. We give you the exact window at hand-back. Light haze or small pockets of moisture while it cures are normal and clear on their own. {{terms:warranty}}
